hooks.text: A Martian volcano builds a cloud longer than Texas.
An eleven-hundred-mile-long cloud vanishes on Mars every single morning.
A Martian volcano spawns a cloud stretching over a thousand miles.

title: The Mysterious 1,100-Mile Martian Cloud
description: Discover the bizarre Martian volcano that spawns a massive water-ice cloud every spring using physics never seen before.

beats.text: A Martian volcano builds a cloud longer than Texas.
beats.visual: Mars Odyssey THEMIS image of Arsia Mons volcano, 2005

beats.text: Arsia Mons stands nearly twelve miles high into the thin air.
beats.visual: HRSC camera image of the Tharsis region volcanoes on Mars, 2004

beats.text: Every spring, it stretches an incredible eleven hundred miles long.
beats.visual: Arsia Mons Elongated Cloud captured by Mars Express VMC, 2018
queries: Arsia Mons Elongated Cloud Mars Express

beats.text: Morning winds lift air fast enough to drop temperatures thirty degrees Celsius.
beats.visual: Mars atmospheric limb view by Mars Odyssey THEMIS, 2006

beats.text: Water vapor freezes directly into ice crystals without dust or particles.
beats.visual: Artist concept of water ice formation in the Martian atmosphere, 2018

beats.text: This exotic physics has never been seen anywhere in a planetary atmosphere.
beats.visual: Mars global view captured by Mars Express HRSC, 2007

beats.text: That is how a Martian volcano builds a cloud longer than Texas.
